text:
Marta: Quick sync — Neptune Health asked for a short performance sprint to validate their triage workflow at scale. Goal: sustained 200 concurrent requests, typical prompt ~120 tokens, and short bursts up to 800 concurrent for ~30s. Need hosted numbers first and a Dedicated delta for cost/SLA.
Dan S.: I can run this on staging. Which model families should I include? rwd-13b-q4_0 for hosted and rwd-13b-fp16 for Dedicated?
Marta: Yes, those two. Also include a quantized dedicated variant if possible.
Ashley: Recommended load shape:
- 5m ramp to 200 (linear)
- 15m steady at 200
- 3 bursts -> 800 for 30s spaced 2m apart
- 10m cool-down
Prime common system prompt before steady phase to warm KV cache. Annotate cold-starts.
Oliver: Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, API error rate, retries, GPU util, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, tokens/s, and per-request token counts. Also capture autoscaler events.
Dan S.: Draft command (wrk-like):
```bash
wrk -t12 -c800 -d00:30:00 --latency \
  -s scripts/openai_style.lua -- https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-q4_0","prompt":"[system] triage \u003c...\u003e","max_tokens":120}'
```
I won't include extra line-continuations in the actual job to keep logs clean.
Marta: Can you output tokens_in / tokens_out per request so Sales can get a $/1M token estimate? Use hosted pricing for hosted runs; for Dedicated, include amortized infra + reserved cost assumptions.
Dan S.: Yep. I'll attach a CSV with per-request tokens and latencies. For batching delta, I'll simulate 1.6x aggregation and show reduced tokens/s and cost impact.
Ashley: Note: autoscaler behavior may add 10-20s latency during shard spin-up on first burst; mark those as cold-start artifacts in the customer deck. Set autoscaler cooldown to 60s for the run.
Oliver: Security note to include in the writeup: hosted has ephemeral keys and standard audit logs; Dedicated offers customer-managed KMS + extended audit retention to satisfy SOC2 vendor review. Add a line in the summary comparing retention windows.
bench-bot: Scheduling run: start_ts=3460014000, lane=staging-small, duration=00:30:00, job_id=neptune-3460. Results will be posted when complete.
Dan S.: Run scheduled. I'll also toggle prefix-caching on/off in separate runs to quantify cache hit improvement.
Marta: Sales asked for a one-slide cost comparison: pilot hosted (3-week pilot), estimated tokens/day and $/month; Dedicated committed (3yr amortized) with SLA note. Keep numbers high-level.
Ashley: I'll own the customer-facing perf writeup and slides. Plan: 1) Executive summary and recommendation; 2) p95/p99 charts and resource usage; 3) cost table (hosted vs dedicated vs hosted+cache+batching); 4) reliability notes and next steps.
Dan S.: Run started at 3460014000. Logs: https://logs.internal/neptune-3460. bench-bot will post a summary.
bench-bot: Run completed at 3460015800. Summary: steady 200 sustained with p95=210ms, p99=480ms for rwd-13b-q4_0 hosted. Bursts to 800 produced transient p99 spikes to ~2.1s due to scale-up. Cache-enabled run showed ~18% token reduction effective and ~12% lower p95. CSV and plots: https://artifacts.internal/neptune-3460/results.zip
Marta: Awesome, thanks. Ashley please take Dan's plots and draft the deck. If there are IP allowlist or key issues, call me immediately. :thumbsup:
Ashley: Will do, aiming to circulate draft slides by end of day tomorrow.
Oliver: I'll add a short appendix with autoscaler logs and KV hit-rate histogram.
Marta: Great work team.
